name: Vessel
tagline: Know what's happening inside you before symptoms show up
description: Vessel is an at-home blood biomarker testing platform that makes preventive health accessible. Users collect a finger-prick sample, mail it in, and receive clinician-reviewed results with actionable wellness plans within 48 hours. No lab visit. No guessing.
mission:
Modern medicine is built around treating sickness, not maintaining health. By the time you feel symptoms, the underlying issue has often been progressing for months or years. Blood biomarkers tell a different story — they reveal metabolic shifts, nutrient deficiencies, hormonal imbalances, and inflammatory markers long before you'd ever think to see a doctor.

Vessel was founded on a conviction that blood testing should be as routine as checking your phone. Not an annual event gatekept by insurance codes and 6-week appointment waits, but a regular practice you do from your kitchen table. We've engineered a clinical-grade dried blood spot collection kit that captures over 40 biomarkers from a single finger prick, processed in our CLIA-certified partner labs with the same rigor as a hospital draw.

But data without context is just noise. Every Vessel report is reviewed by a licensed clinician who translates your numbers into plain language — what's optimal, what needs attention, and what to do about it. We pair results with personalized nutrition, supplement, and lifestyle recommendations that evolve as your biomarkers change over time.

We believe preventive health shouldn't be a luxury reserved for biohackers and concierge medicine patients. Our pricing starts lower than a single copay, and our longitudinal tracking means each test builds on the last, creating a biological timeline that gets smarter the longer you use it.

The healthcare system won't fix prevention. It's not designed to. Vessel is building the infrastructure for a world where understanding your own biology is effortless, affordable, and empowering.
marketResearch:
The global preventive health and wellness testing market is valued at $28B in 2025, with at-home diagnostics growing at 19% CAGR. Direct-to-consumer blood testing is a $2.4B segment accelerating as consumers demand ownership of their health data. The broader consumer health monitoring TAM — including wearables integration — reaches $45B by 2028.

Our SAM focuses on health-conscious adults aged 28-55 in the US who already spend on wellness (supplements, fitness, organic food) but lack objective data to guide decisions. This represents roughly $4.2B in addressable spend. Our initial SOM targets the biohacker-adjacent mainstream — people who use fitness trackers and read nutrition labels — in major metros, approximately $380M.

The competitive landscape includes Everlywell (broad DTC testing, brand awareness but limited longitudinal tracking), InsideTracker (strong science but premium pricing excludes most consumers), and Quest/Labcorp's DTC arms (clinical credibility but terrible UX). Vessel differentiates through three axes: a genuinely painless collection experience with dried blood spot technology, longitudinal tracking that surfaces trends across tests, and clinician-reviewed reports at a price point 60% below InsideTracker.

Our GTM motion is subscription-first. Users start with a comprehensive baseline panel ($79), then subscribe to quarterly monitoring ($49/test). Retention is strong because each test adds context to previous results. B2B channels include employer wellness programs and health coaches who white-label our testing under their practice.

name: Meadow
tagline: Menopause care designed by women who've been there
description: Meadow is a comprehensive menopause care platform combining board-certified menopause specialists, evidence-based treatment plans, and a supportive community. From perimenopause through postmenopause, Meadow provides personalized hormonal and non-hormonal interventions, symptom tracking, and ongoing clinical guidance.
mission:
Menopause affects every woman who lives long enough to experience it — roughly 1.3 billion worldwide by 2030. Yet it remains one of the most undertreated, under-researched, and poorly understood transitions in medicine. The average woman sees three doctors before getting adequate menopause care. Many never do.

Meadow exists because this is unacceptable. We've built a clinical platform purpose-designed for menopause — not a general telehealth service that treats it as an afterthought. Every provider on our platform is a board-certified menopause specialist. Every treatment protocol reflects the latest evidence, not the outdated fear-based guidance that still dominates primary care.

We meet women where they are. Whether you're experiencing your first hot flash at 43 or navigating bone density concerns at 58, Meadow creates a personalized care plan that considers your complete health picture — hormonal therapy when appropriate, non-hormonal alternatives when preferred, and lifestyle interventions that actually move the needle.

But clinical care is only half the equation. Menopause is isolating in a way that few health transitions are. Friends don't talk about it. Partners don't understand it. Meadow's community brings together women at every stage — sharing experiences, asking questions, and proving that this transition can be powerful rather than diminishing.

We're building the menopause care infrastructure that should have existed decades ago. Not incremental improvement, but a fundamental reimagining of how women experience this chapter of their health.
marketResearch:
The global menopause market is projected to reach $24.4B by 2030, driven by the largest generation of women entering menopause in history. FemTech overall is growing at 16% CAGR, with menopause-specific solutions emerging as the fastest-growing subsegment. The US menopause care market alone represents $6.8B, with digital health platforms capturing an increasing share from traditional pharma.

Meadow's SAM targets women aged 40-65 in the US and UK with commercial insurance or willingness to self-pay for specialized menopause care — approximately $2.1B. Competitors include Evernow (telemedicine-focused, limited to HRT prescriptions), Gennev (acquired by Unified Women's Healthcare, broad but shallow clinical depth), Midi Health (strong clinical model but enterprise-only), and Alloy (DTC hormone therapy, pharmacy-forward). Meadow differentiates through comprehensive longitudinal care — not just prescribing hormones but managing the full menopause journey with specialist providers, symptom tracking that informs treatment adjustments, and an integrated community that improves retention.

Our GTM strategy combines DTC acquisition through search and social (menopause content performs exceptionally well on Instagram and TikTok) with B2B2C partnerships with self-insured employers offering menopause benefits. The employer channel is accelerating as companies recognize that menopause-related productivity loss costs $1.8B annually in the US alone.

name: Kairos
description: Kairos is a precision sleep optimization platform that combines clinical-grade sleep diagnostics, circadian rhythm analysis, and personalized intervention protocols. Using data from wearables, environmental sensors, and validated questionnaires, Kairos builds a sleep architecture profile and delivers evidence-based protocols to optimize each stage of sleep.
mission:
We spend a third of our lives asleep, yet treat it as dead time. The sleep industry is split between two extremes: consumer gadgets that count hours without understanding physiology, and clinical sleep labs that are expensive, inconvenient, and designed to diagnose disorders rather than optimize performance.

Kairos bridges that gap. We're building a precision sleep platform grounded in chronobiology — the science of how biological rhythms govern every system in your body. Your sleep architecture isn't random. It follows patterns shaped by your genetics, light exposure, meal timing, stress physiology, and circadian chronotype. Understanding these patterns is the key to sleeping better, not just longer.

Our platform ingests data from the devices you already wear — Oura, Whoop, Apple Watch — and layers in environmental data from our optional bedroom sensor. We analyze sleep staging, HRV patterns, respiratory metrics, and room conditions to build a comprehensive sleep architecture profile. Then we deliver personalized protocols: light exposure timing, temperature adjustments, supplement stacking, breathwork sequences, and meal timing windows calibrated to your unique circadian profile.

We don't believe in one-size-fits-all sleep hygiene tips. The person who naturally peaks at 10pm needs fundamentally different interventions than the person who's sharpest at 6am. Kairos makes that distinction and builds around it.

Our team includes sleep researchers from Stanford's Sleep Epidemiology Research Center, circadian biologists, and engineers obsessed with the intersection of data and human performance. We're here to turn sleep from a mystery into a controllable variable.

Competitors include Oura (excellent hardware, minimal intervention guidance), Whoop (fitness-focused, limited sleep optimization), Eight Sleep (hardware-dependent, temperature only), Sleep Cycle (alarm app, no clinical depth), and Rise Science (circadian tracking but no personalized protocols). Kairos differentiates as a device-agnostic intelligence layer — we work with the wearable you already own and deliver the interventions that none of these platforms provide. Our moat is the proprietary chronotype-matching algorithm that maps individual circadian profiles to evidence-based intervention protocols.

GTM is product-led through integration partnerships with wearable manufacturers. Users connect their device, complete a chronotype assessment, and receive their first protocol within 24 hours. Free tier includes basic sleep scoring; premium ($19/mo) unlocks full protocol generation, environmental optimization, and monthly clinician check-ins.

name: Tendril
tagline: Eat plants with purpose, not guesswork
description: Tendril is a plant-based nutrition planning platform that eliminates the guesswork from eating well without animal products. Using clinical nutrient modeling and real food databases, Tendril creates personalized meal plans that hit every micronutrient target — no supplements required unless you want them.
mission:
Plant-based eating is surging, but nutritional literacy hasn't kept pace. Millions of people are cutting out animal products for ethical, environmental, or health reasons, only to discover that avoiding deficiency is harder than Instagram makes it look. Iron, B12, zinc, omega-3s, complete proteins — the gaps are real, and most meal planning apps treat every diet the same.

Tendril was built specifically for people who eat plants. Not as a filter on a general nutrition app, but as a ground-up platform that understands the unique nutritional landscape of plant-based eating. Our nutrient modeling engine knows that spinach iron isn't the same as lentil iron, that vitamin C pairing increases absorption by 6x, and that a 'complete protein' can be built across a day, not just a single meal.

We create weekly meal plans that are clinically modeled to hit every micronutrient target for your age, sex, activity level, and health goals. Each plan uses real foods from real grocery stores — not obscure superfoods or expensive specialty items. And every recipe is designed to be genuinely delicious, because nutritional completeness means nothing if nobody wants to eat the food.

Our founding team includes a registered dietitian who specializes in plant-based nutrition, a food scientist, and engineers who believe that the most sustainable diet on Earth shouldn't require a PhD to do well. We're building the tool we wished existed when we made the switch ourselves.
marketResearch:
The plant-based food market is valued at $44.2B globally in 2025, growing at 12% CAGR. Adjacent to this, the nutrition app market is $4.8B with meal planning apps specifically representing $1.2B. The intersection — nutrition tools designed specifically for plant-based eaters — is an underserved niche with fewer than five serious competitors and approximately $380M in addressable revenue.

Tendril's SAM focuses on committed plant-based eaters (vegan and vegetarian) in the US, UK, and Western Europe who are willing to pay for personalized nutrition guidance — roughly $620M. Our SOM targets health-conscious plant-based eaters aged 22-45 in urban areas, representing $95M.

Competitors include Cronometer (excellent tracking but no meal planning), Dr. Greger's Daily Dozen (free but simplistic), Forks Over Knives (recipes without nutrient modeling), and general apps like MyFitnessPal (not designed for plant-based micronutrient optimization). Tendril is the only platform that combines clinical-grade nutrient modeling with practical, grocery-store-friendly meal planning specifically for plant-based diets.

GTM is content-led. Plant-based nutrition content drives massive organic search volume, and our free nutrient gap assessment converts curious visitors into users. The freemium model offers basic meal suggestions free; premium ($12/mo) unlocks full weekly plans, grocery lists, nutrient tracking, and seasonal menu rotation. B2B partnerships with plant-based food brands provide sponsored recipe integration and additional revenue.

name: Neura
tagline: Your brain. Your genes. Your formula.
description: Neura creates personalized brain health supplements using genomic data. By analyzing genetic variants that affect neurotransmitter production, methylation pathways, and neuroinflammation, Neura formulates custom nootropic stacks tailored to each individual's neurobiological profile.
mission:
The supplement industry is broken. Walk into any store and you'll find walls of identical pills making identical claims with zero personalization. Meanwhile, the science of nutrigenomics has quietly proven that genetic variants dramatically alter how individuals metabolize nutrients, produce neurotransmitters, and manage neuroinflammation. What works for one brain may be useless — or harmful — for another.

Neura is applying this science to brain health. We start with a simple saliva test that analyzes over 80 genetic variants relevant to cognitive function: COMT and MAO variants that govern neurotransmitter breakdown, MTHFR polymorphisms that affect methylation and B-vitamin utilization, APOE status for neuroinflammation risk, and BDNF variants that influence neuroplasticity.

From this profile, we formulate a custom supplement stack manufactured in our FDA-registered facility. Not a generic multivitamin with a personalization sticker, but a genuinely unique formulation where ingredient selection, dosing, and form (methylfolate vs folic acid, for instance) are determined by your genetics.

We pair the supplement with a cognitive tracking protocol that measures working memory, processing speed, and mood over time — creating a feedback loop between your genomic profile, your supplementation, and your actual cognitive performance. This is how personalized nutrition should work: test, intervene, measure, refine.

Our advisory board includes neurogenomics researchers from UCSF and formulators with decades of experience in evidence-based supplementation. We're not selling brain pills. We're building a precision brain health platform.

Consumers are moving decisively from generic stacks to individualized formulations.

Competitors include Thesis (personalized by questionnaire, not genetics), Nootopia (complex stacks, no genomic basis), Rootine (genetically personalized but focused on general health, not brain-specific), and generic nootropic brands (Alpha Brain, Mind Lab Pro). Our moat is the proprietary neurogenomic-to-formulation mapping built with clinical advisors.

Users order a saliva kit ($149 including first month's supply), receive genomic results and their custom formula in 10 days, and subscribe for monthly deliveries ($69/mo). name: Paloma
tagline: Finally, thyroid care that keeps up with you
description: Paloma is a dedicated thyroid care management platform offering at-home thyroid testing, virtual endocrinologist consultations, and continuous medication optimization. For the 20 million Americans living with thyroid conditions, Paloma replaces the cycle of undertested, undertreated thyroid care with a proactive, data-driven approach.
mission:
Thyroid disease is one of the most common chronic conditions on Earth, yet it remains stubbornly mismanaged. The standard of care — a single TSH test and a levothyroxine prescription — ignores the complexity of thyroid physiology. Millions of patients remain symptomatic despite being told their labs are 'normal,' because no one is testing Free T3, Free T4, TPO antibodies, or reverse T3. No one is optimizing medication based on symptoms, not just reference ranges.

Paloma was founded to fix this. We provide comprehensive thyroid care that starts with the right tests and ends with patients who actually feel well — not patients who merely fall within a lab range. Our at-home blood test measures the complete thyroid panel, not just TSH. Our virtual endocrinologists specialize in thyroid conditions and take the time that a 7-minute PCP appointment never allows.

But testing and consultations are just the beginning. Thyroid care is longitudinal — it requires ongoing monitoring, medication adjustments, and attention to the constellation of symptoms that thyroid patients know intimately: fatigue, weight changes, brain fog, hair loss, mood swings, temperature sensitivity. Paloma's symptom tracking and periodic retesting create a continuous care loop that catches drift before patients start feeling terrible again.

We believe that no one should have to fight their doctor for a complete thyroid panel. No one should be told they're fine when they clearly aren't. Paloma exists because thyroid patients deserve care that's as persistent as their condition.

name: Solace
tagline: Grief doesn't follow a timeline. Neither should your support.
description: Solace is a therapy matching platform designed specifically for grief and loss. Using a detailed intake that considers loss type, grieving style, cultural context, and therapeutic preferences, Solace connects individuals with therapists who specialize in bereavement — not generalists who happen to list it on their profile.
mission:
When someone experiences a significant loss, the last thing they should have to do is become a project manager for their own healing. Yet that's exactly what the mental health system demands: search directories, make cold calls, explain your story to voicemails, wait weeks for intake appointments, and hope the therapist you finally see actually understands grief beyond the five stages model that was never meant to be prescriptive.

Solace was built to eliminate every barrier between a grieving person and the right therapist. Our matching algorithm considers dimensions that generic directories ignore: the type of loss (partner, child, parent, pregnancy, suicide, ambiguous loss), the griever's cultural and spiritual framework, their attachment style, whether they prefer structured or open-ended therapy, and whether they need someone who's experienced a similar loss themselves.

We believe that grief therapy is not general therapy with a sad topic. It requires specialized training — in complicated grief, disenfranchised grief, meaning reconstruction, and continuing bonds. Every therapist on Solace has completed advanced bereavement training and dedicates at least 50% of their practice to grief work. We don't just check a box on a directory. We verify depth of specialization.

Beyond matching, Solace provides continuity. Grief doesn't resolve in 12 sessions. It resurfaces at anniversaries, holidays, and unexpected moments years later. Our platform maintains your therapeutic relationship and makes it easy to return when you need support again — even after a long gap.

Loss is universal. Good grief care shouldn't be a matter of luck.
marketResearch:
The US mental health market is valued at $280B, with therapy and counseling representing $42B. Grief-specific therapy is an underquantified niche, but with 2.5 million deaths annually in the US alone — each affecting an average of 5 close survivors — the population seeking bereavement support at any given time exceeds 10 million. At an average therapy spend of $2,400 annually, the grief therapy TAM is approximately $6B.

Solace's SAM targets adults actively seeking grief therapy who prefer online matching over cold-calling directories — roughly $1.2B. Our SOM focuses on the initial match (where our value proposition is strongest) in top-50 US metros, approximately $150M.

Competitors include BetterHelp/Talkspace (massive scale but no grief specialization), Psychology Today directory (self-service, no quality vetting), GriefShare (peer support groups, not individual therapy), and traditional therapist referrals (slow, limited by personal networks). Solace differentiates through specialization — every therapist is grief-vetted, matching considers loss-specific variables, and the platform is designed for the non-linear nature of bereavement.

GTM is referral-driven. Funeral homes, hospice organizations, and estate attorneys are natural partners who encounter grieving individuals at the moment of need. We provide co-branded resources these organizations can share, driving warm leads. Organic search for grief therapy terms is substantial (400K+ monthly searches in the US). Revenue model: therapists pay a monthly platform fee ($79) plus a per-match fee ($25). No cost to grieving individuals for matching.

name: Kinetic
tagline: Your phone is your physical therapist's eyes between visits
description: Kinetic uses smartphone camera-based motion tracking to monitor physical therapy exercise form, count reps, measure range of motion, and report adherence to care providers. No wearables, no special equipment — just the phone patients already have.
mission:
Physical therapy has an adherence crisis. Studies consistently show that only 35% of PT patients complete their prescribed home exercise programs. The result: slower recovery, repeated injuries, unnecessary surgeries, and billions in avoidable healthcare spending. The core problem isn't motivation — it's that patients go home with a printout of stick figures and no feedback on whether they're doing the exercises correctly.

Kinetic turns any smartphone camera into a real-time exercise coach. Using computer vision and pose estimation, our app tracks joint angles, movement speed, range of motion, and form quality as patients perform their prescribed exercises at home. Reps are counted automatically. Form deviations trigger gentle corrections. Progress is logged and shared with the prescribing PT in real time.

But we're not replacing physical therapists — we're extending their reach. Kinetic gives PTs visibility into what happens between visits, replacing the unreliable 'How did your exercises go this week?' with actual data: adherence rates, range of motion trends, and flagged form issues that need attention. Clinicians can adjust programs remotely based on objective progress data instead of patient self-report.

Our founding team includes a sports medicine physician, a computer vision researcher, and physical therapists who saw firsthand how much clinical value was being lost in the gap between visits. We believe the phone in every patient's pocket is the most powerful rehab tool nobody's using.

The goal isn't to make physical therapy virtual. It's to make home exercises actually work.
marketResearch:
The physical therapy market is valued at $45B in the US alone, with the digital MSK (musculoskeletal) health segment growing at 28% CAGR to reach $8.4B by 2028. Home exercise program compliance is the single largest driver of PT outcomes, yet existing solutions (paper handouts, generic exercise video libraries) haven't moved adherence above 35% in decades.

Kinetic's SAM targets PT clinics and health systems seeking to improve home exercise adherence and demonstrate outcomes to payers — approximately $2.8B. Our SOM focuses on progressive PT practices (5+ clinicians) and hospital-affiliated outpatient rehab programs in the US, roughly $400M.

Competitors include Hinge Health ($6.2B valuation, employer-focused MSK, requires sensor), Kaia Health (app-based exercise guidance, limited motion tracking), SWORD Health (sensor-dependent, enterprise-only), and MedBridge (exercise library, no motion tracking). Kinetic differentiates as the only camera-only solution that provides real-time form feedback, objective adherence data, and clinician-facing dashboards — with zero hardware cost to patients or clinics.

GTM strategy is clinic-led. PTs prescribe Kinetic alongside their exercise programs. Patients download the free app. Clinics pay $199/month per clinician for the provider dashboard, adherence analytics, and EHR integration. Enterprise contracts with health systems and payers add remote therapeutic monitoring (RTM) billing support, which creates a direct reimbursement pathway for providers using the platform.

name: Bloom
tagline: What's growing inside you matters more than what you eat
description: Bloom is a gut microbiome testing and personalized meal planning platform. Using shotgun metagenomic sequencing, Bloom maps the bacterial species in your gut and creates meal plans designed to cultivate a healthier microbiome — reducing inflammation, improving digestion, and supporting immune function through food, not pills.
mission:
The gut microbiome is arguably the most important organ system that medicine still barely understands in clinical practice. Research has linked microbiome composition to everything from autoimmune disease and depression to metabolic health and cancer treatment response. Yet when a patient presents with IBS, bloating, fatigue, or skin issues, the standard medical response hasn't changed in decades: try elimination diets, take a probiotic, see if it helps.

Bloom is building the bridge between microbiome science and everyday nutrition. We use shotgun metagenomic sequencing — not the cheaper 16S rRNA method — to identify bacterial species in your gut at strain-level resolution. This matters because two people might both have Lactobacillus, but at different strains with completely different functional roles.

From your microbiome profile, we generate a personalized meal plan designed to shift your gut composition toward a healthier state. Not through restrictive elimination or expensive supplements, but through strategic inclusion of prebiotic fibers, fermented foods, and polyphenol-rich ingredients that feed the specific beneficial species your gut needs more of — and starve the inflammatory ones you have too much of.

Our science team includes microbiome researchers from the Human Microbiome Project, registered dietitians, and food scientists who translate genomic data into recipes you'll actually want to cook. We believe the gap between cutting-edge microbiome research and patient benefit can be closed with better technology and better food.

The gut isn't just a digestive organ. It's a garden. Bloom helps you grow the right things.
marketResearch:
The gut health market is valued at $53B globally, with microbiome testing growing at 22% CAGR as consumer awareness of the gut-health connection accelerates. The DTC microbiome testing segment alone is $1.8B, while the broader gut-health nutrition market (probiotics, prebiotics, functional foods) reaches $19B. The intersection — testing-informed personalized nutrition — represents approximately $3.2B in addressable opportunity.

Bloom's SAM targets health-conscious adults experiencing digestive issues who prefer food-based solutions over supplements — roughly $1.5B in the US. Our SOM focuses on women aged 25-50 with IBS, bloating, or inflammatory symptoms in metro areas, approximately $220M.

Competitors include Viome (microbiome testing with supplement recommendations, not meal planning), ZOE (blood sugar + microbiome, meal scores but not full plans), Floré by Sun Genomics (custom probiotics, not food-based), and Thryve (microbiome testing with generic probiotic recs). Bloom differentiates by being food-first — we don't sell supplements as the primary intervention. Our meal plans are clinically designed to reshape the microbiome through dietary fiber diversity, fermented food integration, and strategic polyphenol intake.

GTM combines DTC acquisition through gut-health content marketing with partnerships with functional medicine practitioners and registered dietitians who want to incorporate microbiome data into their nutrition counseling. Revenue: initial test kit + report ($189), meal plan subscription ($14.99/mo), retest kits ($149) recommended quarterly to track microbiome shifts.

faqs.question: How is this different from Viome or ZOE?
faqs.answer: Viome and ZOE are excellent products with different approaches. Viome focuses on supplement recommendations; ZOE focuses on blood sugar response. Bloom is food-first — we create full meal plans designed to reshape your microbiome composition through dietary changes, not supplements.

faqs.question: Why shotgun sequencing instead of 16S?
faqs.answer: 16S identifies bacteria at the genus level — like knowing someone is 'American.' Shotgun metagenomics identifies species and strains — like knowing their name and what they do for a living. The clinical recommendations we can make at strain-level resolution are dramatically more specific.

faqs.question: Do I need to give up foods I love?
faqs.answer: Bloom is about adding, not restricting. We focus on increasing dietary fiber diversity and fermented food intake while incorporating polyphenol-rich ingredients. You won't be eliminating food groups unless there's a specific clinical reason.

faqs.question: How quickly will I see changes in my microbiome?
faqs.answer: Dietary shifts can begin changing microbiome composition in as little as 48 hours, though meaningful, stable shifts typically take 6-12 weeks. We recommend retesting at the 3-month mark to see progress.

name: Aegis
tagline: Rare disease patients deserve more than rare options
description: Aegis is a clinical trial matching platform for patients with rare diseases. By integrating electronic health records, genetic test results, and a comprehensive global trial database, Aegis identifies eligible clinical trials that patients and their physicians would otherwise never find — reducing the average rare disease diagnostic odyssey from 7 years of searching to days of matching.
mission:
There are over 7,000 known rare diseases affecting roughly 400 million people worldwide. For most, there is no FDA-approved treatment. Clinical trials represent the only path to potential therapy, yet fewer than 5% of rare disease patients ever participate in one. The reason isn't lack of trials — it's that patients can't find them, and trials can't find patients.

Aegis exists to solve the matching problem. A parent with a child diagnosed with a rare mitochondrial disorder shouldn't need to become a medical researcher to discover that a Phase II trial at a hospital 200 miles away is enrolling patients with exactly their child's genetic mutation. Yet that's the reality today — trial recruitment relies on physician awareness (which is spotty), ClinicalTrials.gov (which is impenetrable for non-experts), and patient advocacy groups (which are fragmented).

Our platform ingests patient health records, genetic test results, and diagnosis codes, and matches them against a continuously updated global database of rare disease clinical trials. We understand the nuanced eligibility criteria that make rare disease trials uniquely complex: specific genetic variants, biomarker thresholds, prior treatment history, and geographic constraints. Our matching engine doesn't just find trials — it pre-qualifies patients against inclusion and exclusion criteria, dramatically reducing the back-and-forth that delays enrollment.

For pharmaceutical sponsors, Aegis solves the existential challenge of rare disease drug development: finding enough patients. We partner with biotech companies running rare disease trials to accelerate enrollment timelines that often stretch years beyond projections, threatening the viability of programs that could bring life-changing therapies to patients with no other options.

Every rare disease patient is searching for hope. Many clinical trials are searching for patients. Aegis connects the two.
marketResearch:
The rare disease drug development market exceeds $209B in annual revenue, with the clinical trial recruitment segment valued at $2.1B. Rare disease trials face the most acute recruitment challenges in pharma — the average rare disease trial takes 2.5x longer to enroll than common disease trials, and 80% fail to meet enrollment timelines. This delays treatments, increases costs, and in many cases kills programs that would otherwise succeed.

Aegis's SAM targets pharmaceutical and biotech companies sponsoring rare disease clinical trials (approximately 2,800 active trials globally), representing $1.4B in recruitment spend. Our SOM focuses on US-based sponsors and CROs running Phase I-III rare disease trials, roughly $350M.

Competitors include TrialSpark (general trial matching, not rare-disease specialized), Antidote Technologies (patient matching, acquired by Precision Medicine Group), Clinical Trial GPS (physician-facing, limited patient engagement), and disease-specific registries (fragmented, single-disease). Aegis differentiates through rare disease specialization — our matching engine handles the genetic variant-level specificity that general platforms miss, and our patient-facing tools are designed for the unique complexity of rare disease populations.

GTM is dual-sided. Patient acquisition comes through partnerships with rare disease advocacy organizations (NORD, Global Genes, disease-specific foundations) and genetic testing companies who can surface matching opportunities at the point of diagnosis. Sponsor revenue comes from per-trial matching fees ($50K-200K depending on disease prevalence) and enrollment success bonuses. We've launched with partnerships covering 14 rare disease indications.
